newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Dollar idles in afternoon Asia, sterling off highs.
newsitem.headline: Dollar idles in afternoon Asia, sterling off highs.

text.p: The dollar continued to waver in a tight band on Monday with nothing to look forward to in afternoon Asian trade as holidays in Tokyo and London severely restricted liquidity.
The British pound was off its early highs as players squared their long positions, with sterling/mark sales weighing on dollar/mark as well, dealers said.
"Sterling/mark was a little bit on the buy side this morning but since then, it's been drifting down," a U.S. bank dealer said, adding, however that the cross should hold above 2.8000.
"I see sterling/mark higher. 2.8200 should be no problem, but not today," he said.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl's statement that Europe's single currency, the euro, would be introduced on schedule was largely ignored by the market.
"Maybe the market is fed up with this EMU (European monetary union) thing. Nothing happened," a European bank dealer said.
Dealers said the dollar looked healthy on the whole after the release of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report and news of a balanced budget accord.

The U.S. Labor Department reported that payrolls rose 142,000 in April, well below the 211,000 rise expected in a Reuters poll, but the unemployment rate fell to 4.9 percent -- its lowest reading in 23 years.

"The U.S. numbers seem to have shown there's not too much to worry about in terms of a rate hike but with it being good news for the stock and bond markets, it's good news for the dollar as well," another European bank dealer said.
The dollar was expected to remain well entrenched in a range of 1.7260-1.7330 marks and 126.50-126.90 yen for the rest of the Asian session.
